title.narrative: Integrated humanitarian assistance to returning internally displaced people in Amuru woreda of Horo Gudru Wellega

description.narrative: ltpgtThe Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus - Development and Social Services Commission (EECMY-DASSC), Swiss Church Aid (HEKS/EPER), and Gurmuu Development Association (GDA) are proposing an ltbgtintegrated multi-sector lifesaving interventionlt/bgt to support conflict-affected voluntary returnees and host communities in Amuru woreda of Horro Guduru Wollega, Oromia Region. Notably, EECMY-DASSC, HEKS/EPER, and GDA are among the few, if not the only, organizations with a ltbgtstrong operational presencelt/bgt in Horro Guduru Wollega. The intervention will focus on six sectors: ltbgtAgriculture, MPCA, WASH, Shelter, Health and Protection,lt/bgt with each organization leading one or two sectors and contributing its experience, resources, and staff in a complementary manner. The project design is informed by a pre-intervention ltbgtMulti-Sector Needs Assessmentlt/bgt (Annex 1) conducted in October 2025. The assessment includes a dedicated section on ltbgtReturnee Dynamicslt/bgt and an accompanying ltbgtRisk Management Frameworklt/bgt to ensure that assistance targets voluntary returnees in accordance with humanitarian standards. Developed in consultation with communities, sector offices, and other humanitarian actors, the proposed intervention will support 24,403 conflict-affected voluntary returnees and 13,668 host community members. Among them, 1,712 persons with disabilities will be reached. A total of ltbgt38,071 persons (19,497 F, 18,574 M) lt/bgtwill be reached.lt/pgtltpgtAmuru woreda has experienced significant damage to lives, assets, and infrastructure from conflict, leaving its population vulnerable and underserved. The project partners, with an established local presence, consulted communities and authorities to identify priority sectors for response. As a result, six urgent sectors were selected for immediate intervention.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe project will fully align with the ltbgtEHCT Position Paper on Returns and Relocationslt/bgt (dated 29 February 2024) and the Cross-Cutting Directive. It will ensure that support to returnees is based on voluntary return in accordance with humanitarian definitions, with careful follow-up on return and relocation processes.ltbrgtThis integrated response is in line with relevant Cluster and Humanitarian Response Plan Objectives. Beneficiary targeting will be fair, transparent, and inclusive, with robust feedback and complaint mechanisms established at community level. The agriculture component will support 7,476 people through the distribution of seeds and tools, agricultural training, restocking of small ruminants, and animal vaccination campaigns. MPCA will provide direct cash assistance to 550 extremely vulnerable returnees, in line with Ethiopia Cash Working Group guidance and post-distribution monitoring standards. The WASH component will include rehabilitation of one key water schemes and construction of two latrines in healthcare facilities, alongside WASH NFI distributions and hygiene promotion efforts, reaching 12,059 people. In response to severe shelter needs, emergency repair kits will be distributed to support 1,568 individuals. The Protection component will reach 645 high-risk individuals through field-level protection monitoring, referral services, and targeted cash assistance. The Health intervention will reach 20,000 persons, led by Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs), will provide essential services, alongside health messaging and hygiene promotion and 2 damaged health facilities will be rehabilitated to restore local health systems.ltbrgtA ltbgtRisk Management Planlt/bgt has been developed for this intervention (Annex 2). The project was designed in close coordination with the relevant ltbgtUN Clusterslt/bgt, whose technical inputs and feedback are reflected in Annex 6. The proposed intervention is fully supported by local government authorities. Careful consideration has also been given to complementarity with ongoing humanitarian responses in the area, including other initiatives funded by CERF/CBPF.lt/pgt
